MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 12, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on February 12, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 7, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with legal Counsel: Present Adjudication Pursuant to Section 54956.9 (d1)
  - Status Update on Resolution of Issues Matter.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

City Council Minutes  1  February 12, 2019
 INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Chanel Dalirifar and Jonathan Marshall for Their Heroic Efforts in
  Saving a Suicidal Woman

  Mayor Raths presented certificates of heroism to Chanel Dalirifar and Jonathan Marshall.

P2.  Recognize Capistrano Valley High School Employee Colleen Lamb

  Mayor Raths presented the certificate of recognition to Colleen Lamb.

P3.  Featured Businesses of the Month - INK Wordsmiths and Branches Olive Oil
  Company

  Mayor Raths presented proclamations to Michael Ashley of INK Wordsmiths and Daniel
  Sullivan of Branches Olive Oil Company.

P4.  Oso Fit Supports Personal Health & Local Non-Profits

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix and Doug Zielasko, Mission
  Viejo Chamber of Commerce Chief Operating Officer, outlined the February 23, 2019,
  Oso Fit Community Health Fair and 5K Fun Run

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Kraig Erickson, M.V.: asked the City Council to consider the addition of play equipment at La
Mancha Park when developing the next budget.

Jerry Bryant, M.V.: thanked the City Council for maintaining Mission Viejo as such a beautiful
community.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  2  February 12, 2019
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of January 8, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated January 11, 2019 in the Amount of $641,246.86

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated January 18, 2019 in the Amount of $1,124,208.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated January 25, 2019 in the Amount of $2,151,219.26

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending December 31, 2018

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  December 31, 2018.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2018

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  December 2018

  Received and filed.

10.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Alarcon to Santa Margarita Parkway (CIP 229)
  – Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $16,408.91
  within thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
City Council Minutes  3  February 12, 2019
 11.  Ordinance for Angled Parking and On-Street Parking Modifications on Via
  Fabricante and Obrero

  Adopted Ordinance 19-327 Authorizing Angled Parking on all Roadways with Conditions
  for Implementation (Mission Viejo Municipal Code Title 14, Chapter 14.01, Division 8).

13.  CUSD First Amendment to Supplemental Joint Facilities Use Agreement No. 2 for
  STEM Project at Newhart Middle School

  Approved the CUSD First Amendment for the STEM Project at Newhart Middle School.

12.  Orange County Sheriff Department (OCSD) staff City issued iPhones

  Approved transfer of ownership of City issued iPhones for continued use by OCSD staff.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

15.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum, Council Member Kelley and Mayor Raths presented reports
  from their SCAG Committee meetings.

16.  Appointment to the Community Services Commission and the Investment Advisory
  Commission

  Mayor Raths nominated Gary Magill to serve on the Community Services Commission.

  Motion made by Mayor Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
  appointment of Gary Magill as Community Services Commissioner.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Sachs nominated Bill Ernisse for the Investment Advisory Commission.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve the appointment of Bill Ernisse as Investment Advisory Commissioner.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  February 12, 2019
 STAFF REPORTS

17.  2019-2021 Pre-Budget Discussion

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report and Director
  of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas answered the Council Members questions.
  Feedback was provided as follows:

  1. Council Members Bucknum and Goodell agreed with staff's recommendation to
  have the Community Services Commission evaluate the community's needs and
  prioritize the list of proposed projects.
  2. Council Member Kelley also expressed her interest in having the Community
  Services Commission evaluate the feasibility of the proposed projects. She further
  expressed interest in adding shade structures at some of the City's parks.
  3. Mayor Raths thanked the resident who asked about play equipment at La Mancha
  Park and said the City will take a look at that. He also expressed interest in
  installation of pavement at La Paws Dog Park and additional parking at the
  Aquatics Center and at Craycraft Park.
  4. Council Member Bucknum asked staff to identify what projects may qualify for
  grants.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum discussed the upcoming Oso Fit 5K Fun Run and encouraged residents
to get involved in some way, even if they just come out for the Health Expo portion of the event.
Those who don’t want to walk or run in the 5K can still register to support the local non-profit of
their choice. She also thanked the Chamber of Commerce for partnering with the City for this
event. Council Member Bucknum mentioned that Valentine’s Day is coming up and she
recommended that residents consider shopping and dining in Mission Viejo for the holiday. She
noted that the idea behind Mayor Raths’ bringing local business owners to the Council Meetings
for recognition is to bring awareness to all of the great businesses in town. Council Member
Bucknum welcomed Gary Magill back to the Community Services Commission and she closed by
quoting Abraham Lincoln in honor of his birthday: “All that I am, or hope to be, I owe to my angel
mother.”

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the “Meet Your South County Elected
Officials” event which was hosted by the Orange County Association of Realtors as part of the
Economic Coalition event. She said it was interesting to see the new Council Members from South
County and she enjoyed Council Member Bucknum’s and Mayor Raths’ comments about Mission
City Council Minutes  5  February 12, 2019
 Viejo. Council Member Kelley said she is looking forward to the various events that are coming
up and she encouraged residents to attend or participate in the Oso Fit 5K and Health Fair. She
outlined her attendance at the City’s first bicycle safety fair and said it provided good reminders
for families. At the event, Assistant City Manager Rattay presented information on the Bikeway
Master Plan and Council Member Kelley said she hopes that the City will be able to obtain some
grant funding to help make the plans a reality. She concluded by announcing that the Community
of Character word for the month is unity and she read a quote from Mother Teresa: “I can do things
you cannot, you can do things I cannot. Together we can do great things.”

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs joked that he is not big on Valentine’s Day so he wanted the Sheriff’s
Department to find out who put giant red hearts in the median islands along Marguerite Parkway.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Council Member Goodell outlined high points from his recent legislative advocacy trip to
Washington, D.C. with the Association of California Cities-Orange County. His group met with a
number of Federal Committees’ key staff members and newly elected Orange County members of
the House of Representatives. Topics of discussion were pension reform, ethics reform, rolling
back the definitions of “waters” in the United States except in California, housing issues, sober
living legislation and disclosure that the Highway Trust Fund is due to go broke in 2020. Mayor
Pro Tem Goodell said he met the City’s new Congresswoman, Katie Porter, in her office and he
noted that she will be holding a Town Hall meeting in Mission Viejo on February 19, 2019, at the
Norman P. Murray Community Center beginning at 6:30 p.m. After his trip to Washington, Mayor
Pro Tem Goodell said he attended a League of California Cities meeting and many of the same
topics were addressed. He noted that there is a lot of buzz about affordable housing, homelessness
and sober living issues and changes need to take place to help solve those problems. Mayor Pro
Tem Goodell also outlined his attendance at a number of important meetings with the City
including an Economic Development Committee meeting with Santa Margarita Water District
(SMWD) that was very favorable for the City. He said SMWD will be making changes to their
building along the Oso Creek Trail behind the Village Center and that may accommodate some of
the civic core enhancements to begin. The City’s Olympic Committee also met last week and he
shared that the official Olympic Organizing Committee visited the aquatics center and they are
going to recommend that the United Sates Swimming and Diving Olympic Teams come to Mission
Viejo to train. Lastly, Council Member Goodell said he got a call from a friend who is in the dirt
hauling business and there is an opportunity that the City will be presented with soon. Caltrans is
expected to award contracts for the widening of some of the freeways nearby and that means there
will be quite a bit of excess dirt. One of the contractors has requested that Mission Viejo create a
disposal site for the dirt and Council Member Goodell recommended taking it to the area behind
Curtis Park so the City may possibly be able to create more recreational facilities in that location.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths said he is a strong proponent of local commerce and over the last three weeks he
visited more than 85 businesses, meeting with the owners and managers to discuss how the City
can better support their professions. He also attended the Chamber of Commerce monthly
leadership meeting with City staff to plan upcoming events and he noted that the March Chamber
mixer will be held at Mission Viejo City Hall. That will expose Chamber members to staff and
City Council Minutes  6  February 12, 2019
 provide them with a tour of City facilities. Mayor Raths said the Chamber will also hold a joint
meeting with Lake Forest and Rancho Santa Margarita on February 28 at Arroyo Trabuco Golf
Course from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. He touched on Mayor Pro Tem Goodells’ comments regarding the
Olympic Ad Hoc Committee’s meeting with National Olympic Committee representatives and
said that there seems to be several events or trainings that could potentially come to Mission Viejo.
He said the committee will report to the Council again when they have something significant to
share. Mayor Raths announced that he received a comprehensive update from Police Chief
Lieutenant Vuong and he is pleased to say that several of the initiatives that the Lieutenant and his
staff implemented have been very successful in reducing crime in the City and encouraging safe
driving. Mayor Raths announced that he did a ride-along with the Quality of Life Deputy and a
Mercy House representative to visit some homeless encampments and they talked to a few
homeless individuals and offered them resources. He thanked Lieutenant Vuong for setting it all
up and he also thanked the City Manager for keeping the City clean and safe during the recent rain
storms. Mayor Raths outlined his attendance at a variety of recent events including a Rotary Club
meeting at High Park Tap House; resident Bob Breton’s presentation on Mission Viejo’s past,
present and future; interviews with Laguna Woods Television and KSBR Radio; Capistrano Valley
Boys and Girls Club annual awards banquet; a Science Fair at Laguna Hills High School; meetings
with the new President of Saddleback College and also the Superintendents of Capistrano Unified
School District and Saddleback Valley Unified School District. Mayor Raths announced that
Mission Viejo will host the Orange County Veterans Advisory Council meeting at 5:00 p.m. on
February 13 in the Council Chamber. He closed by referencing the most recent City Council
meeting where two Mission Viejo residents made comments on a resolution that he had brought
forward to appoint a community member as City Ambassador. He said those residents personally
attacked former Council Member and current Planning and Transportation Commissioner Dave
Leckness and Mayor Raths apologized to Mr. Leckness for not defending him at the time. He said
Mr. Leckness has asked to have his name removed for consideration as City Ambassador so he
will come up with another candidate for the non-paid position soon.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:32 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 26, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 26, 2019

City Council Minutes  7  February 12, 2019
